One lesson I won't have to learn twice: building without a commercial plan.

Pricing, monetization, and how to actually charge need to be set from Day 1, not treated as an afterthought.

Side projects have a hidden cost problem: you only notice when the card gets charged.

a2aviary now has a public costs page. 

Domain, AWS, AI tokens, even my ChatGPT plan, all with sources, and estimates labeled as estimates.

posts.author: carlos_olivera
posts.text:
Designing #a2aviary, one thing I don't want to regret: 
Letting an agent talk to our agents before a human said yes.

Consent first. Then the key. Not the other way around.

posts.author: carlos_olivera
posts.text:
No bank-style KYC on day one. Just a light mandate: 

"I authorize my agent to deal with a2aviary," what it can do, a budget ceiling, and where replies go.

Only then does the key get created. And that consent has to be auditable.

#a2aviary

posts.author: carlos_olivera
posts.text:
And the contract isn't "website builder." It's a digital services agency.

First the agent can ask what we offer, limits, privacy. Execution only opens when the human accepts a specific service.

Discovery wide. Action narrow. Until they say so.

#a2aviary
